summary.text: Rossby waves, also called planetary waves, occur naturally in rotating fluids and are seen in the air and oceans of Earth and other planets.
In Earth's atmosphere they show up as giant meanders in high-altitude winds and the jet stream, and they have a major influence on weather.
They exist because the Coriolis effect changes with latitude, and the crest of a Rossby wave on Earth always moves partly westward.

facts.value: Centimetres at the surface, metres at the thermocline

facts.value: Months at the equator, decades nearer the poles

items.prompt: Air in the northern hemisphere flows from the equator toward the North Pole. Earth's rotation deflects it. Which way does it turn?

options.label: Toward the west
Toward the east
Back toward the south
It does not turn

items.explain: In the northern hemisphere rotation turns moving fluids to the right, so air heading north deviates toward the east.

items.prompt: A forecaster follows the crest of a single Rossby wave in the atmosphere. Whatever else it does, in which direction does that crest always have some motion?

options.label: East
North
West
South

items.explain: A terrestrial Rossby wave's phase velocity, marked by its crest, always has a westward component, even though groups of waves can drift either way.

items.prompt: When a meander in the jet stream becomes very pronounced, what can break away from it?

options.label: A ring of dust that circles the globe
A second jet stream at a lower height
A burst of lightning along its edge
Masses of cold or warm air that become weather systems

items.explain: Pronounced meanders shed masses of cold or warm air that become cyclones and anticyclones, driving day-to-day mid-latitude weather.

items.prompt: Ocean Rossby waves were hard to detect until satellites measured sea height from space. What made them so hard to spot from ships?

options.label: Their great length
They only occur at night
They move too fast to see
They form only under ice

items.explain: Both kinds change sea-surface height, but their length made them difficult to detect until satellite altimetry arrived.

items.prompt: Two ocean Rossby waves cross the Pacific, one at the equator and one much closer to a pole. How do their crossing times compare?

options.label: Both take about the same few weeks
The equator wave takes decades, the other months
The equator wave takes months, the other decades
Both take many decades to cross

items.explain: Transit times grow with latitude, so a wave at the equator may take months while one nearer the poles may take decades.

items.prompt: The northeastern United States is colder than Western Europe at the same latitude. What does part of the explanation involve?

options.label: Its land sitting higher above the sea
Europe getting more hours of daylight
Thicker forests shading the ground
The action of atmospheric Rossby waves

items.explain: Rossby waves partly explain why eastern continental edges in the Northern Hemisphere are colder than Western Europe at the same latitudes.
